obligation.description: In ReadOnlySafe mode with a non-singleton active voter configuration, a heartbeat response carrying a completed prior request context must not be credited as an acknowledgment of a different pending request context, or by that credit alone cause the later request ReadState to be released before its own quorum confirmation.

assumptions: Fresh caller context bytes uniquely identify the later invocation.

grounding.derivation: Node.ReadIndex promises a request-specific read state and requires context discipline; ReadOnlySafe obtains authority through quorum communication. The source test describes heartbeat responses attached to a read context as the majority acknowledgment of leader authority and expects completed context records to be freed. The local requirement is that support labeled for a completed context is not silently credited to a distinct later invocation. It does not require a read to complete when responses are missing. The two-voter scope makes one leader self-ack insufficient and permits an independent test of an old response before the fresh follower response arrives.
grounding.applicability: Use distinct immutable nonempty contexts under ReadOnlySafe after current-term commitment. Both old reply production and later request are in one serialized public RawNode history. The monitor will preserve the necessary direction: no fresh read output when only stale-context support has been delivered, then a completed fresh-control path after its genuine response.
unresolved: A bounded public-API replay schedule must still execute.
alternatives: A same-context retry could refer to the same logical invocation, and the API has version-qualified rules; that different scope is deliberately not inferred here.
